Criteria detail:
- A concept is a term of the course subject: a thing the subject has a name for, such as a technology, device, component, method, process, quantity, property, principle, or a named system, standard or model.
- It is what a student would look up in glossary/index of textbook on subject, and node in concept map.
- Concepts used to find facts about a term when student asks, link lectures, build maps/exercises.
Requirements:
1. From facts only. Take every concept facts name. Do not add concept facts do not name.
2. Terms of subject, not ordinary words. Take a term of subject even when facts only mention it while teaching something else. Leave out ordinary words and descriptions that facts only use to say something ("the real world", "the user", "a problem"). Leave out a source that is only named as where a statement comes from (dictionary, report, survey). A named product, system, person or organisation is a concept only when a fact says something about it that belongs to subject.
3. One concept per thing. If facts use several names/wordings for same thing, one concept. A thing and a kind of it, a thing and a part of it, and a thing and a property of it are different concepts.
4. Name: full words, singular, lower except proper names, no article/acronym.
5. Aliases: every other name facts use, written as in facts: acronym/abbreviation and other wordings. Most have one/none.
6. Facts: numbers of all facts that name concept: facts that say something about it, and facts that use it to say something about another concept. Every concept has at least one fact, every fact should belong to at least one concept.
7. Defined true when facts teach what concept is: one defines it, or says what it consists of or how it works, so student could answer what is it. False when only mention: use to teach something else, or say something about it without saying what it is.

We have course title etc but facts only matter. Need extract concepts from facts [1]-[6]. Segment goal: Describe four broad steps of tracking process: calibration, registration, integration, drift correction.

Facts:
[1] There are two broad ways to obtain input for tracking: inside-out and outside-in.
[2] The tracking process broadly consists of four steps: calibration, registration, integration, and drift correction.
[3] In the tracking process, calibration is the step that transforms the output of imperfect sensors so that it behaves as closely as possible to the natural or real value, reducing sensor error.
[4] In the tracking process, registration estimates or determines the initial position and orientation of the sensor, so that the starting point is known before movement can be tracked.

Facts:
[1] The choice of how to track, and which tracking method or technique to apply, depends on tracker position, tracking process, and tracker types.
[2] Based on the position of the tracker or sensor that provides input for tracking, tracking is categorized into outside-in tracking and inside-out tracking.
[3] In outside-in tracking, the user's experience device does not contain the tracking sensors or trackers; instead, external trackers or sensors in the real world, such as cameras or markers, provide data that helps the system attached to the user identify and track the user's motion, pose, and orientation.
[4] Most virtual reality (VR) headsets today that use external sensors fall under outside-in tracking.
[5] Outside-in tracking is restricted to the specific area where its external sensors are placed and works only when the user is in that environment within the sensor range, whereas inside-out tracking has no such restriction because the user wears the sensors or the sensors are attached to the user.
[6] Inside-out tracking is a tracking type in which the cameras or other sensors required for tracking are located within the device used for the experience, such as the head-mounted display (HMD) in virtual reality (VR), which is more common, so no other external devices are needed.
[7] Examples of inside-out tracking are Microsoft HoloLens, Intel Project Alloy, and Qualcomm VR820.
